Sept mille and quinze mille on Belmas I p172 spell 7,000 British and 15,000 Spanish. Expedition concentration, explicitly disputed against other population scopes.
Environ neuf mille on Belmas III p667 spells about 9,000 garrison under Menacho, excluding armed inhabitants. It is not the numerically identical later surrender population.

Belmas I p175 prints 21 mars. Frozen endpoint is 20 March; inspected Oman IV p255 describes conditional terms on the following day after the 19th, with twenty-four hours for relief. Agreement/delivery distinction retained, not silently changed.
Cinq cents on Belmas I p188 spells 500 entering with Rovira on night 9–10 April. Entry party is distinct from Toreno’s approach components and Bodart available population.
Dix mille on Belmas I p189 spells 10,000 in Campoverde’s relief force, a French enemy estimate distinct from Spanish components and fortress garrison.
Quarante-cinq mille on Belmas I p177 spells 45,000 concentrated around Almeida, excluding militia and Spanish bands. Not a dated actual-engaged total.

Près de vingt mille on Belmas I p182 spells nearly 20,000; composition continues from p181, which was also inspected. Narrative force, not a dated original return.
Près de vingt mille on Suchet II p22 spells nearly 20,000 besiegers, explicitly including artillery/engineers. Original appendix not independently inspected.

Toreno IV p279 prints 25 for Dorsenne’s attack; frozen Bodart/Belmas comparison is 24, directly inspected on Bodart p426 and Belmas I p196. Uncertain army/division crosswalk preserved.
Vingt à vingt-deux mille on Suchet II p147 spells 20,000–22,000 in the 15-September situation. Antecedent expedition availability only, not 25-October local strength.
Vingt à vingt-deux mille on Suchet II p147 spells 20,000–22,000 in the 15-September situation after distant garrison deductions; not all close-siege troops.
Oman IV p602 prints 28th and header Oct.28; screen does not match ordinal 28th to 28. Frozen comparison 27 is directly inspected on Bodart p428. Date alternative retained.

Trente- at end Suchet II p209 continues trois mille at start p210, spelling 33,000. Same inspected p209 dates Reille’s Segorbe arrival 24 décembre and states Pannetier still behind; cited two-page count is concentration, not all engaged.

Toreno IV p322 prints 9 de enero and the chapter context spans end-1811/January1812; Suchet II p227 prints 1812 at the margin and dates army departure 10 janvier. Frozen 9-January1812 endpoint remains unchanged.
